non_blocking_findings: THE CAP BOUNDS THE CATASTROPHE BUT DOES NOT REACH 5 SECONDS AT THE CONTRACTED VALUE. C1's 2048 was justified on a SINGLE measured sample (1,429ms / 168 output tokens). Repeated sampling shows that sample was unrepresentative: at 2048 the same question with one prior turn took 5370ms, 4610ms and 19299ms, emitting 1153, 1170 and 2048 output tokens. The story's live check expects a follow-up under 5 seconds; 2048 will not meet that reliably. The implementation matches the approved contract exactly and every leaf passes, so this is recorded rather than unilaterally changed.

THE CAP NEVER TRUNCATES, AND LOWER IS BETTER. Every run at 256, 512 and 2048 returned stopReason tool_use with a valid tool block - the model emits the tool call and then continues producing text, so output saturates at whatever cap is set and the cap simply cuts the waste. More headroom is therefore strictly worse, which inverts C1's stated 'headroom' reasoning. Measured: 512 gives 2667-5833ms, 256 gave 1162ms and 2681ms. A one-constant change to LLM_SELECTOR_MAX_TOKENS is the obvious follow-up.

ONE SAMPLE AT 256 RETURNED unsupported for a harder question (MIS statement by leaf across two months) at 114 output tokens - below the cap, so not truncation. It may be a legitimate refusal or model variance; a single sample is not evidence either way, and 512 answered the same question with a selection.
D-0024 and D-0031 remain open, so every leaf was judged by its testcase name and executed count rather than an exit code.
